issues.body: `_invokes_command` remains `token in line.split()`. Shell quotes are syntax removed before argv reaches Python, while `str.split()` preserves the quote characters. Thus `run: python3 scripts/account-usage.py "--persist-limits" usage.json` invokes persistence, but the reader sees `"--persist-limits"` and returns false; the same applies to single quotes. If a second workflow uses either ordinary spelling, `_workflows_invoking` omits it and `serialization_premise_errors` can still return empty. The new reader tests include comments, prose, suffixes, and unquoted tokens, but no quoted exact flag, so they do not detect the bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Parse executable shell text with a shell-aware lexer so quotes are decoded before exact argv-token comparison, with explicit handling for the supported command separators and continuations. Add synthetic second-workflow tests using both double-quoted and single-quoted `--persist-limits`; assert each workflow is enumerated and `persist_limits` refuses before any `gh` call.
issues.title: Quoted persist flags still bypass workflow invocation discovery

verdict.summary: The round-3 major remains unchanged. `_invokes_command` still uses plain whitespace splitting, so shell-quoted spellings of `--persist-limits` are invisible even though the shell removes those quotes and passes the exact flag to Python. The added invocation-reader cases still exercise only unquoted flags. Consequently, a second workflow can invoke persistence with an ordinary quoted flag while `_workflows_invoking` omits it, allowing `serialization_premise_errors` to report that the single-writer premise holds. No new finding is needed, but the existing trust-plane bypass remains major.
